summary: A public statement by Public Key Partners about public key standards and licenses. It is informational only and not an Internet standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC is a public statement from Public Key Partners about patents covering public-key cryptography. It lists four patents and says licenses for RSA signatures will be available on reasonable, non-discriminatory terms.

questions: what patents cover public key cryptography
which public key patents did public key partners list
what licensing terms did public key partners offer for rsa
subtitle: A public statement on licensing patents related to public-key cryptography.

tldr.problem: The memo addresses how interested parties could license patented public-key methods, including RSA digital signatures.
tldr.mechanism: Public Key Partners lists four patents for which it received exclusive sublicensing rights and assures readers that RSA signature licenses will be available on reasonable, non-discriminatory terms.
tldr.outcome: The memo records the company's licensing statement and says it is informational, not an Internet standard.

today: RFC 1170 is Informational and records Public Key Partners' statement about public-key patent licensing in January 1991. It does not specify an Internet standard.

sections.title: Patents Listed in the Memo
sections.content:
Public Key Partners says MIT and Stanford granted it exclusive sublicensing rights to four patents in the United States and corresponding foreign patents. The listed inventions are Diffie-Hellman, Hellman-Merkle, RSA, and Hellman-Pohlig.

The memo says these patents cover all known methods of practicing public-key cryptography, including variations known as El Gamal.
sections.plainLanguage: The statement lists four patents and says they cover known public-key methods, including El Gamal variations.

sections.title: Assurance About RSA Licenses
sections.content: Public Key Partners endorses incorporating RSA into a digital-signature standard. It assures interested parties that licenses to practice RSA signatures will be available under reasonable terms and conditions on a non-discriminatory basis, in line with the stated policies of ANSI and IEEE.
sections.plainLanguage: The company says it will make RSA signature licenses available on reasonable terms that do not discriminate between users.

sections.title: Status of the Memo
sections.content: RFC 1170 is an informational public statement by Public Key Partners. The memo says it does not constitute an Internet standard.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC records a company's statement about licensing. It does not define an Internet standard.
